after.title: INSPIRE therapy for canine liver tumors
after.center: NC State College of Veterinary Medicine
after.status: Enrolling dogs with liver tumors; posted enrollment finish July 1, 2027
after.funding: 🟢 Fully funded. The protocol flyer lists oncology consultation, bloodwork at each study visit, multiple CT scans, echocardiogram with EKG, liver-tumor fine-needle aspirate with pathology, and possible liver lobectomy as study benefits.
after.notes: Current official protocol states enrollment through July 1, 2027, superseding the previously published July 1, 2026 finish. Dogs need 1–2 liver tumors measuring 1–8 cm, weight at least 30 lb and a cytological diagnosis before screening. Metastasis, any other cancer, major heart disease or arrhythmia exclude participation. Group 1 receives one INSPIRE treatment followed by liver lobectomy one week later; group 2 receives up to three treatments at three-week intervals and five CT/bloodwork follow-ups over nine months. The official flyer specifies fully funded consultation, study bloodwork, CT scans, echocardiogram/EKG, tumor aspirate/pathology and possible liver lobectomy. Study-team eligibility screening remains required.

reason: Explicit current primary enrollment finish extended to 2027; complete protocol and funding flyer reviewed.

before.title: Fully funded CAR-T cell therapy trial for canine B-cell lymphoma
before.center: LEAH Labs / University of Minnesota / Ohio State University / University of Missouri
before.status: Missouri enrolling per current institutional protocol; Ohio State enrolling per sponsor with local slot to confirm; Minnesota on hold
before.contacts: LEAH Labs — info@leahlabs.com; enrollment request form on the official site
before.funding: Missouri: study-related initial staging, treatment and rechecks covered; up to$4000 for adverse events and a$2000 stipend for future/additional VHC treatment upon completion. Sponsor describes Ohio enrollment as fully funded; confirm the current Ohio coverage and slot. Minnesota is on hold; its historical stipend/criteria are not generalized to other sites.
before.notes: One LEAH CAR-T protocol with site-specific cohorts. On October16 the current Missouri study-specific invitation and fresh Web read both explicitly confirm enrolling dogs with spontaneous CD20+ large-cell B-cell lymphoma; the older cached Missouri ON HOLD version is superseded. Missouri includes naive and relapsed patients, >10kg, clinically well, no primary GI or lung involvement, investigator bloodwork clearance, no Apoquel/mycophenolate/cyclosporine/azathioprine and at least72hours off prednisone. It combines lymphodepleting chemotherapy and xenogeneic CAR-T; at least seven visits over21days then longer follow-up. Minnesota current individual protocol remains On hold; its10-50kg and48hour rules must not be generalized to Missouri. Ohio remains enrolling per sponsor; its current institutional index does not name this protocol, so confirm the Ohio slot and local criteria before travel. Missouri-specific eligibility/funding do not establish Ohio or Minnesota terms.

after.title: Fully funded CAR-T cell therapy trial for canine B-cell lymphoma
after.center: LEAH Labs / University of Minnesota / Ohio State University / University of Missouri
after.status: Missouri enrolling per institutional protocol; Minnesota open and enrolling per institutional protocol; Ohio enrolling per sponsor, local slot to confirm
after.contacts: LEAH Labs — info@leahlabs.com; enrollment request form on the official site
after.funding: Minnesota: scheduled study visits including screening fully funded; $2000 future UMN cancer-care credit upon completion or welfare-related early departure, and up to $4000 severe CAR-T-related medication support at UMN. Missouri: study staging, treatment and rechecks covered, up to $4000 adverse-event allowance and $2000 completion stipend for future/additional VHC care. Ohio coverage and current slot require confirmation.
after.notes: One LEAH CAR-T protocol with site-specific cohorts; conditioning chemotherapy is mandatory. The current Minnesota institutional protocol explicitly says Open and enrolling, superseding its previous hold. Minnesota: at least 10 kg, no Boxers; peripheral multicentric high-grade CD20+ B-cell lymphoma, at least four evaluable nodes, naive or relapsed substage A disease, performance status 0–1; no listed immunomodulators; Cytopoint allowed; at least 72 hours off prednisone and remain off. Missouri remains enrolling under its current protocol with distinct >10 kg/no primary GI or lung involvement criteria. Ohio remains enrolling per sponsor; confirm its local slot and eligibility before travel. Do not generalize any site-specific criterion or funding allowance to another site.

sites.hospital: University of Minnesota College of Veterinary Medicine
sites.status: Open and enrolling — current institutional protocol
sites.eligibility: Dogs at least 10 kg, any breed except Boxers; peripheral multicentric lymphoblastic/high-grade CD20+ B-cell lymphoma with at least four evaluable peripheral nodes; naive or relapsed substage A disease; performance status 0–1. No Apoquel, mycophenolate, cyclosporine or azathioprine. Cytopoint permitted. Prednisone must not be for substage B disease, must stop at least 72 hours before CAR-T and remain stopped.
sites.funding: Scheduled study visits including screening fully funded; $2000 future UMN cancer-care credit on completion or welfare-related early departure; up to $4000 severe CAR-T-related adverse-event medication support when care is at UMN.
sites.schedule: Pentostatin days -5 to -2, cyclophosphamide day -3; intravenous and intranodal CAR-T day 0; follow-ups days 7/21 and months 2/3.

after.special_requirement: Study-team screening and conditioning chemotherapy required. Minnesota: >=10 kg, no Boxers, peripheral multicentric high-grade CD20+ B-cell lymphoma, >=4 evaluable peripheral nodes, naive/relapsed substage A, performance status 0–1 and >=72-hour prednisone washout. Missouri: >10 kg, clinically well, no primary GI/lung involvement and >=72-hour prednisone washout. Confirm Ohio criteria and slot.
